correctness.rationale: The periodic diagonal D gives W=gamma DSD^{-1} with ratios uniformly bounded above and away from zero. Below and above unit geometric mean, orbit norms respectively vanish and diverge (the latter for nonzero vectors only). At gamma=1, S^n tends weakly to zero, as is seen by testing against the tails under (S*)^n. On residue r the orbit norm squared is exactly Q_r(x), so the limiting squared displacement is ||x||^2+Q_r(x). The tail of a minimizing progression is syndetic for every strictly enlarged tolerance, including at the boundary radius; below the minimum a sufficiently small enlargement leaves at most finitely many returns. This proves the exact sublevel description, including x=0. Independently evaluating the two phase forms gives (34/25,1) at A, (1,23/20) at B, and ((107+2 sqrt(14))/100,(67+4 sqrt(14))/80) at their midpoint, with both midpoint entries greater than 1. W is power bounded by 2 but ||We_1||=2. This is an exact counterexample, not a numerical orbit inference. The frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed; the conclusion uses the symbolic proof and exact arithmetic.
